name: Sahel insurgency
summary: JNIM and IS Sahel attacks on state forces continue; no capital or major city has fallen or been newly blockaded
state: Jihadist groups continue to attack state forces across Mali, Burkina Faso and Niger; the most recent large attack found was on a Malian army base, reported on 14 Sep, in which at least 50 soldiers were killed (Africanews). Searches on 16 Nov found no new fall or blockade of a capital or major city and no new mass-casualty attacks spreading to coastal states, so Watch holds.
for_you: People in central and northern Mali, Burkina Faso and western Niger are most exposed to attacks and displacement. Travellers should follow FCDO advice, which warns against all travel to most of the region. Spillover risk is highest in the northern border areas of Benin and Togo.
rubric_hit: Sustained insurgency at current levels (Watch); no capital blockade or spread of mass-casualty attacks to coastal states

sources.title: Africanews — At least 50 soldiers killed in jihadist attack on Malian army base

why: Jihadist groups control growing territory across Mali, Burkina Faso and Niger, driving displacement and coastal-state spillover.
drivers: JNIM/IS-Sahel offensives, juntas, Russian forces, blockades, coastal-state attacks.

rubric.alert: Blockade or fall of a capital or major city, or mass-casualty attacks spreading to coastal states.
